competences: The learner states facts about the capital city.
The learner explains points related to Symbols of a nation: the capital city.
languageCompetence: Reads, spells and writes: capital city, kampala, administrative centre.
objectives: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to state the facts about the capital city.
By the end of the lesson, learners should answer original sourced questions on Symbols of a nation: the capital city.
priorKnowledge: Learners have previously learned about Uganda as an independent nation. They extend their knowledge to the capital city.
materials: Primary Five Social Studies notes covering Symbols of a nation: the capital city
references: P.5 Social Studies Lesson Notes Term III: Uganda as an Independent Nation

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher links the previous study of Uganda with The capital city. They ask "Which was the capital city of the colonial government?" and listen to the children's replies before introducing the new subject points.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners recall the previous work and answer the introductory question in full sentences based on prior knowledge.

steps.stage: Development: Meaning and key facts about the capital city
steps.content: Kampala is the capital city of Uganda. Kampala Capital city Authority. (KCCA) Medical services. Important places in Kampala A national capital city is the main administrative centre in the country. It’s the administrative centre. The capital city of Uganda is Kampala It is an educational centre Important buildings found in Kampala Entebbe was the colonial capital city of Uganda. Qn: Why was the capital city of Uganda transferred from Entebbe Kampala is centrally located. Qn: Name the body that governs Kampala city .
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes the recorded facts about The capital city on the board, including "Kampala is the capital city of Uganda.; Kampala Capital city Authority. (KCCA)". The teacher asks learners to explain each important term and checks their answers against the source.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the factual points, respond to teacher questions and copy the notes clearly into their Social Studies books.

steps.stage: Development: Features and other facts about the capital city
steps.content: It’s the centre for communication Its the centre education. It’s the biggest commercial centre. A commercial centre is a place where people can buy goods and services. Services provided by a commercial centre. St Balikudembe market Rubaga catholic church etc DIVINE EDUCATION CENTRE:0784540287/0751565742 Page 10 It serves as an administrative centre It serves as the main administrative centre The national capital city
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes the recorded facts about The capital city on the board, including "It’s the centre for communication; Its the centre education.". The teacher asks learners to explain each important term and checks their answers against the source.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the factual points, respond to teacher questions and copy the notes clearly into their Social Studies books.

steps.stage: Development: Further details about the capital city
steps.content: A capital city of a nation serves as the centre of all the major activities of a country. It serves as a commercial centre It is a communication centre. The state house International conference centre Bank of Uganda It crosses Greenwich town in England Qn: Name the capital city in Africa which crossed by the Greenwich He opened up the first shop in Kampala He built fort Edward at old Kampala and raised the IBEACO flag
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes the recorded facts about The capital city on the board, including "A capital city of a nation serves as the centre of all the major activities of a country.; It serves as a commercial centre". The teacher asks learners to explain each important term and checks their answers against the source.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the factual points, respond to teacher questions and copy the notes clearly into their Social Studies books.

steps.content: Which was the capital city of the colonial government? | Why should a nation have a national capital city? | Why is Kabale cooler than Kampala? | What title is given to the political head of capital city authority ? | When did Uganda get her independence?
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher sets the sourced exercise, beginning with "Which was the capital city of the colonial government?" and "Why should a nation have a national capital city?". They move around the class to assist learners and correct responses using the supplied lesson notes.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners answer the source questions in their books, compare answers with the notes and correct errors after feedback.

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher reviews the key facts on The capital city, asks "Which was the capital city of the colonial government?" and then checks understanding with "Why should a nation have a national capital city?". They conclude by assigning the remaining sourced exercise for revision.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners give oral answers, state one main fact from the notes and correct their exercises before the lesson ends.

assessment: Mark written responses to the sourced questions, including "Which was the capital city of the colonial government?" and "Why should a nation have a national capital city?", and ask learners to explain their answers using the recorded points.
homework: Complete the lesson's original sourced exercise, including "What conference was the climax of all Uganda’s struggle for independence?"
